title: Regiment and Orchard
premise: In 1893, on a storm-battered Cornish coast, widowed lighthouse keeper Gideon Yarrow has buried his past so thoroughly that even he half-believes the quiet life he built. When census taker Miriam Quill notices a name crossed out in the old parish register, she unknowingly unravels the secret Gideon has kept for twenty years: he once promised a Prussian sailor, Elias Brandt — now declared an enemy alien as war fever rises — safe passage and shelter if ever he came ashore. When Elias's daughter arrives shipwrecked and hunted, Gideon must choose between the law, the village that trusts him, and a promise made in peacetime. In the end, Gideon shelters her through the great storm, loses the lighthouse but keeps his integrity, and discovers that identity is not what we hide but what we honor.
about_author: Xanthe Iversen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing coastal parish records and lighthouse logbooks in Cornwall. Their fiction is known for spare prose, tidal pacing, and characters who keep their hardest truths just below the waterline.

chapters.title: The Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Gideon Yarrow's POV. Census taker Miriam Quill arrives at the lighthouse during a rising gale; her routine questions turn sharp when she spots a foreign name inked into Gideon's late wife's prayer book. Gideon deflects, but that night he opens a locked sea chest he hasn't touched in twenty years. Emotional beat: the first crack in twenty years of careful silence.

chapters.title: What the Register Kept
chapters.summary: Miriam's POV. Back in the village, Miriam cross-references the register and finds a marriage record with a page torn out — and learns the torn page concerned a Prussian sailor witnessed by one 'G. Yarrow.' Her superiors, stirred by anti-German feeling, ask her to report anomalies. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into complicity; Miriam hesitates over the reporting form.

chapters.title: A Promise Made in Peacetime
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, moving into extended flashback to 1873: young Gideon, then a merchant sailor, wrecks off the Prussian coast and is saved by Elias Brandt. The two men swear an oath of mutual shelter — 'if ever your people call mine enemy.' Emotional beat: warmth and dread braided together, as we learn exactly what Gideon stands to lose.

chapters.title: The Girl on the Rocks
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. After a violent night storm, Gideon finds a half-drowned young woman in the rocks below the light — Lena Brandt, Elias's daughter, fleeing detention as an enemy alien after her father's death. She carries her father's half of the oath, written on oilcloth. Emotional beat: terror and recognition; the promise has come due.

chapters.title: Silences That Keep People Safe
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Hidden in the lamp room, Lena learns the rhythms of Gideon's solitude and the shape of his grief for his wife, Edith. She begins to understand which silences protect him — and which ones are strangling him. Meanwhile, a coastguard patrol sweeps the headland. Emotional beat: fragile trust forming between two people built of secrets.

chapters.title: The Village Weighs Its Keeper
chapters.summary: Miriam's POV. Rumors spread of lights answered from the sea; Miriam, sent back to investigate, recognizes Lena's coat drying by the stove and says nothing — yet. The village blacksmith, whose son died at sea, demands action against 'foreigners.' Emotional beat: Miriam torn between duty, conscience, and her growing respect for Gideon.

chapters.title: Interrogation at the Harbour Inn
chapters.summary: Alternating Gideon and Miriam POV. Miriam confronts Gideon privately; he tells her most of the truth, trusting her with the oath but not yet with Lena's presence. She warns him the navy will search the lighthouse within days. Emotional beat: two guarded people choosing each other's side without quite saying so.

chapters.title: The Great Storm Rises
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The worst storm in living memory makes landfall; the navy's search is delayed but a wrecked trawler signals distress, and among its crew are men who will recognize Lena. Gideon must run the light, hide Lena, and prepare rescue lines all at once. Emotional beat: everything converging; no more room left for silence.

chapters.title: The Oath Kept
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating Gideon, Lena, and Miriam POV. During the rescue, a crewman denounces Lena; Miriam publicly declares her own testimony — that Lena was pulled from the wreck as a survivor, nothing more — and burns her report. Gideon nearly dies securing the line, saved by Lena's hands. Emotional beat: sacrifice, witness, and the cost of promises honored in full view.

chapters.title: Regiment and Orchard
chapters.summary: Resolution, Gideon's POV. The inquiry strips Gideon of his post, but the villagers — led by the blacksmith, shamed by the storm — stand for him. Lena stays through spring, tending the abandoned orchard behind the keeper's cottage, before sailing to join kin abroad. Gideon plants Edith's roses beside her trees. Emotional beat: belonging rebuilt not as safety from memory, but as peace within it.
